entries.what: A restore scope keyed to a symptom
entries.detail: Item 408 selected its 52 pages by the Day 3/10/30 string and missed florida.html and florida-expansion.html, which carried the same stale composer without that string. Scope is derived from the market set, never from a string found in the damage.

entries.what: Zero Google was only as wide as the pattern that measured it
entries.detail: Every "zero Google" statement this week searched for google.com/search. Nine Google News RSS links sat in florida-expansion.html throughout, in 26a7ad6 and in 4e5d5bc; the stale copy that masked them did so by accident. STOP 6 found on day one what four sweeps missed. A clean result proves the pattern, not the estate.

American Fasteners to Modern Distribution Management and FreightCenter to FreightWaves, both the outlets cited; Alpha Foundations, Palm Medical Centers (two links) and Altitude Water (two links) to the issuer’s own release, with the issuer’s date; Health Network One (Heyward Donigan) and STS Aviation Group (Mark Smith): no Wayback snapshot of either Google News URL, link struck, rows stay Unverified, note reads “Decision maker read 2026-10-31; source link unresolvable; re-verification required.”

entries.what: A Copy rich button nobody could reach
entries.detail: The composer overlay did not scroll; on a 720 px screen Copy rich sat at 724–780 px, and the rebuild would have pushed it off a 900 px screen. The overlay now scrolls (Ruling 19).

entries.what: The consoles carried a composer two days older, and read the wrong market
entries.detail: The 27 consoles still carried the 4 Nov composer, so one-composer parity had failed since fa20114 changed the market pages alone. They now carry the one rebuilt composer. The composer took its market from the page name, so on a console it read “console-florida”: Florida’s console signed Timothy and linked poster2-console-florida.html, a page that does not exist (live, before this item). The market now drops the console- prefix; console-florida signs Edward E. Edick and links Florida’s pages.

entries.what: The end-to-end test asserted the retired forms
entries.detail: Two expectations predated the rulings: the Florida signer as “Edward Edick” (now Edward E. Edick, Ruling 8) and an Outlook web URL without the mailbox segment fa20114 introduced. Two expectations were corrected to ruled forms before the run; the 32 of 32 is a pass against the rulings, not an independent confirmation of them.

entries.what: Standing rule: a composer change is complete only at 81 of 81
entries.detail: fa20114 changed the market pages only, so one-composer parity was broken from 05:48 on 6 November and no check caught it — the second partial sweep in this programme to read clean. A composer change is not complete until all 81 pages carry it, proven by count in the same pass; parity at 81 of 81 with zero deviations is the gate.

entries.what: A verification that disagrees, then agrees on retry
entries.detail: Nine files disagreed on first read. Three were proven identical by commit-pinned re-read; six were cleared only by a second full read on the same path. A verification that disagrees, then agrees on retry, establishes agreement — not that the first disagreement was spurious.

entries.what: Part A: every index figure counted by one stated method, its definition on its line
entries.detail: index_measure.py counts every index figure from the 27 working and 27 expansion files: 3,804 Verified rows; 3,747 Verified companies estate-wide by the stated company rule (legal forms kept), with 3,708 shown beside it if a trailing legal form is folded (39 fewer); 1,343 expansion rows, 409 Verified; 4,132 dialable rows at Tier A or B, qualifier verbatim; 42 call-ready rows carrying an address in the Email column. Struck: 3,721, 902 / 902, 4,139 / 4,050, 327 / 320 and the acquisition backlog of 182. All 27 cards remeasured. gate.py STOP 7 (exit 8) re-counts all 90 figures at zero tolerance.

entries.what: My own company count read the sector line as part of the name
entries.detail: The 3,794 put to the Chair (and the 3,798 and 3,796 before it) counted the whole Company cell, which carries the sector line beneath the bold name, so one company with two sector lines counted twice. Counted by the bold name alone the figure is 3,747. Found while re-deriving the 13 tier contradictions, which reproduce only when the name is read alone. A count whose definition is not on the page hid a fault in the counter itself.

entries.what: Three company counts wrong by one cause (Chair, verbatim)
entries.detail: Three published company counts were wrong by the same cause: the counter read a cell containing the name and the sector line, so one company under two sectors counted twice. None of the three was caught by reviewing the number. It was caught by re-deriving an unrelated heading from the rows.

entries.what: A ruling made on a generalisation (Chair)
entries.detail: Recorded from the Chair’s close brief: the ruling for 3,708 rested on the builder’s sentence that all 39 folds were the same company inside one market, a generalisation from twelve checked by hand; measured, 37 sit inside one market and 2 span two. The ruling is replaced by 3,710 and 3,708 is struck from the page. Ruling 2 (3,794) is withdrawn, not restated: it ruled on a counter’s output without asking what the counter read. #55’s Hold is sustained.

I reported “all 39 merges are the same company within the same market” after checking twelve. The twelve were; the claim was about thirty-nine. Two pairs span two markets: Central Distributors (Michigan) and Central Distributors, Inc. (Tennessee); Torcon (New Jersey) and Torcon PA (Pennsylvania), where PA may mean the state. A sample described as the whole is an untraceable figure in a sentence.

entries.what: Item 413 close: what the index now proves
entries.detail: Headline 3,710 Verified companies (a trailing legal form folded only where both forms occur inside one market), 3,747 as the stated alternative (legal forms kept); 3,708 struck. Part B: “4 settled” did not reproduce and is struck; “13 tier contradictions” reproduces as 18 by the stated company rule and is corrected, with its definition on the page; 9 held pairs, 8 still differ in tier, Rosboro Company now reads Tier C in both files and its printed Tier B (oregon.html row 70) is corrected to C; Illinois and Chicago printed “verified-callable is 0”, the rows give 1 Verified row with an address in the Email column in each, corrected; both register-ingest notes (119 / 112, 3 → 22; 57 / 56, 68 → 78, 67 → 76) had no derivation and are struck; the Florida practice line is computed when the page loads and says so. STOP 7 re-counts 96 figures and the printed held-pair tiers at zero tolerance and measures all four company rules on every run.

entries.what: A commit that landed and gated clean, but did not deploy
entries.detail: ab311bf (Item 413-A) is on main with all five Part A files byte-exact against the package, and gate.py check on it exits 0 with all seven stops clear (STOP 7 90 of 90). GitHub Pages run 427 (pages build and deployment, id 42250846987) for ab311bf completed with conclusion FAILURE, reporting 2 errors, 1 warning and 3 notices; the annotation text needs a signed-in GitHub session and was not read. Pages kept serving the index from the previous successful run (426): Last-Modified 6 Nov 2026 16:11:07 GMT, still showing the struck 3,721. This is a deploy fault, not an upload fault: the fix is a re-run of the deploy or the next commit’s deploy, not new files. The gate reads the repository, not the served site, so it could not see this; nothing in the programme yet checks what Pages serves.

entries.what: Seven stops measured the repository; none measured the served site
entries.detail: Seven integrity stops measured committed bytes and none measured the served site. A failed deploy left a struck figure on the live page while the gate read exit 0. An instrument that passes cannot be assumed to be answering the question it is trusted to answer.

A deploy check read a run’s conclusion without bounding the read to the run in question, and returned the previous run’s success. The same fault as entry 16, found inside the check built to prevent it. A bounded read is part of the measurement, not a refinement of it.

entries.what: Item 415: the archive invariant resolved, restated and guarded
entries.detail: The invariant read “archives every row Tier C and none Verified” without saying what Status means. Two readings were defensible: Status as the row’s standing (every one of the 27 Verified archive rows moves to Downgraded), or Status as whether a decision maker was found (the four Florida rows with sourced decision makers stay Verified; the 23 with none move). The estate decided it: 2,205 of the 2,282 Tier C rows in the working and expansion files read Downgraded, so Status records standing. The rows were wrong, not the invariant; the invariant is restated in florida-standard.json so it cannot be read the other way, and gate.py STOP 9 (exit 10) re-reads all 1,376 archive rows against it. entries.what: A rule derived from the rows (Chair)
entries.detail: Two readings of a field were both defensible from its wording. The estate was measured — 2,205 of 2,282 comparable rows — and the measurement decided which reading the system actually held. A rule derived from the rows outranks a rule asserted over them.
